X.note: Top half of the frame is empty sky. The ground is a flat orange plane with a few scattered props: a cannon, cannonball piles and barrels. The soldiers are peg-doll figures with no proper bodies. The white block buildings are plain boxes with slab shadows and no real Georgian or Genoese character. The Union Flag is a mismatch for the period. It is the post-1801 design, whereas Gibraltar in 1782 would fly the 1707 flag (Union Jack without the St Patrick's cross). The scene is clean and calm, but it looks like a simple 3D mockup.

Y.note: An aerial view of the town with real terrain, water, hills, defensive walls and clustered terracotta roofs. It reads as an actual place and gives a sense of scale and geography. The trees are low-poly blobs, the grass is a bit smeared and the town is fairly generic. Heavy overlay captions (four text boxes) crowd the frame and the bottom-left caption covers part of the scene. It is still a convincing, informative explainer frame, and the caption text is legible with no garbled lettering.

why: Y shows a believable, geographically readable 3D town with real terrain and water, while X is a sparse toy-like set under a mostly empty sky.
top_fix_for_weaker: Crop or lower the camera so the buildings and ground fill the frame, and cut the empty sky. Replace the peg-doll soldiers with properly modelled 1780s redcoats. Fix the flag to the pre-1801 Union flag. Add texture and clutter to the ground and facades (cobbles, shutters, balconies, tiled roofs, stacked stores, people) so it reads as Gibraltar's Grand Parade.
